chapter: Touring, band and money in the 1950s-60s
title: Being recorded unknowingly at WMRY for five dollars
summary: His first record was cut at the radio station without his knowing it was a recording, paid five dollars and released without a contract.

bands.name: Sugar Boy and His Cane Cutters

story.theme_name: Getting paid for records: royalties, publishing and flat fees
story.community_name: Royalties, publishing and who owns the song

blocks.x: You mean he did the record and when you walked out he gave you five dollars?
He gave me five dollars.
Who, who gave me a lot of chess games?
Five dollars? And we was just as happy, we didn't know what was going on. And that was for the whole band?
Band members get five dollars each?
No, we got five dollars. For the whole band? Right. Five dollars.
Wow.
We went around a couple of blocks away. Bought us some red beans and rice and got us some wine. That was it. In fact, I didn't know the record was going to be released. Nobody did, really.
We made that record in the studio, in the radio station.

W.R. Wilde on Josephine Drys. Josephine. Oh, you mean M-O-Y. Oh, W-M-O-Y. Yeah. And, uh, well I was just sitting and, uh, we used to go up there and rehearse all the time. And, uh, we was in there and, uh, the guy said he wanted to see how we sound playing something that, uh, we made up. So, we played that.
Was the flag shots?

Yeah. And he said, uh, he said, uh, I want to see how you sound on the microphone. So, okay. So, I sung and I played it. And he said, okay. So, that was it. So, when we finished, he told me, he said, I might have a surprise for you. And, he gave me five dollars. So, I thought maybe he was coming back later, you know, and record. And, about a month later, a month after that, this jockey, earned it a whip, called me up and told me to come to the radio station and have a surprise for me. And, I went out there and there, it was my record, Sugar Boy and Can Cutters.
I just don't know what I'll do.
Right. I didn't even know that I was being recorded.
So, you just thought that was a demo?
Okay.
I didn't, I didn't know, I didn't know it was anything, really.
You didn't even know they were recording. So, you hadn't signed a contract with Chester before?
No, I hadn't. I hadn't signed a contract either.
So, he really, really, really stolen, hadn't really had your consent to release it.

Right. He, uh, in fact, uh, See, uh, the radio station used to be on the air from, uh, maybe, uh, like, six o'clock in the morning until around six o'clock in the evening. Right. And, uh, the radio station.
Was that the station that Papa Staple went on?
No.
No, that's M.O.Y. That's, it was, it was.

And, uh, the radio station would go off the air at six o'clock. And, uh, like we started rehearsing around that time, you know? And, uh, this is what happened. They had a whole lot of people in the radio stations. And now, usually there are no people in, uh, in the recording studio when you are recording, you know? And try to keep it quiet as you can. But, that wasn't the case this time. And people in there, and they were just sitting around. Of course, nobody said anything, you know? Nobody made any noise or anything like that. But, that's the way it went.
Mm-hmm.
